title: Advice of Vasishta to Bharata
introduction: Vasistha advises Bharata to stop lamenting and to perform the last rites of the king. Bharata then places the body of Dasaratha on a couch, taking it out from the vessel where it had been immersed in oil and proceeds with the funeral rites. The appointed priests, attendants, people of the city and the weeping royal women followed the funeral pile of the king to the banks of Sarayu River where the body was cremated. Bharata along with others return to the city after the completion of the cremation-ceremony.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्सप्ततितमः सर्गः
Thus completes 76th Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
तम् एवम् शोक सम्तप्तम् भरतम् केकयी सुतम् |
उवाच वदताम् श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठः श्रेष्ठ वाग् ऋषिः
verses.iast:
tam evam śoka samtaptam bharatam kekayī sutam |
uvāca vadatām śreṣṭho vasiṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭha vāg ṛṣiḥ
verses.translation: The sage Vasishta, the excellent one among the speakers having eloquence, spoke to that Bharata, Kaikeyi's son who was thus tormented with grief.

verses.devanagari:
अलम् शोकेन भद्रम् ते राज पुत्र महा यशः |
प्राप्त कालम् नर पतेः कुरु सम्यानम् उत्तरम्
verses.iast:
alam śokena bhadram te rāja putra mahā yaśaḥ |
prāpta kālam nara pateḥ kuru samyānam uttaram
verses.translation: "O, the greatly illustrious prince! My blessing to you. You have lamented long enough. Perform in an excellent way, the last rites of the king."

glosses.meaning: the greatly illustrious one! bhadram = blessing

verses.devanagari:
वसिष्ठस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भरतः धारणाम् गतः |
प्रेत कार्याणि सर्वाणि कारयाम् आस धर्मवित्
verses.iast:
vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutvā bharataḥ dhāraṇām gataḥ |
preta kāryāṇi sarvāṇi kārayām āsa dharmavit
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Vasishta, Bharata conversant with his duty fell prostate and proceeded with all the arrangements for the obsequies.

verses.devanagari:
उद्धृतम् तैल सम्क्लेदात् स तु भूमौ निवेशितम् |
आपीत वर्ण वदनम् प्रसुप्तम् इव भूमिपम्
सम्वेश्य शयने च अग्र्ये नाना रत्न परिष्कृते |
ततः दशरथम् पुत्रः विललाप सुदुह्खितः
verses.iast:
uddhṛtam taila samkledāt sa tu bhūmau niveśitam |
āpīta varṇa vadanam prasuptam iva bhūmipam
samveśya śayane ca agrye nānā ratna pariṣkṛte |
tataḥ daśaratham putraḥ vilalāpa suduhkhitaḥ
verses.translation: Raising the body of king Dasaratha, from the vessel where it had been immersed in oil, seeming as it were asleep with face in the color of gold, that son Bharata placed it in a magnificent couch, adorned with every kind of precious stone and in a great grief, lamented.(as follows):

glosses.meaning: where it had been immersed in oil
with face in the color of gold
adorned with energy kind of precious stone

verses.devanagari:
किम् ते व्यवसितम् राजन् प्रोषिते मय्य् अनागते |
विवास्य रामम् धर्मज्ञम् लक्ष्मणम् च महा बलम्
verses.iast:
kim te vyavasitam rājan proṣite mayy anāgate |
vivāsya rāmam dharmaGYam lakṣmaṇam ca mahā balam
verses.translation: "O, king! Having sent into exile the virtuous Rama and Lakshmana who is possessed of great strength, while I was away from home and had not yet returned, what did you intend to do?"

verses.devanagari:
क्व यास्यसि महा राज हित्वा इमम् दुह्खितम् जनम् |
हीनम् पुरुष सिम्हेन रामेण अक्लिष्ट कर्मणा
verses.iast:
kva yāsyasi mahā rāja hitvā imam duhkhitam janam |
hīnam puruṣa simhena rāmeṇa akliṣṭa karmaṇā
verses.translation: "Where will you go, leaving this person (me) who was distressed and bereft of Rama the unwearied one in action and the excellent one among men?"

verses.devanagari:
योग क्षेमम् तु ते राजन् को अस्मिन् कल्पयिता पुरे |
त्वयि प्रयाते स्वः तात रामे च वनम् आश्रिते
verses.iast:
yoga kṣemam tu te rājan ko asmin kalpayitā pure |
tvayi prayāte svaḥ tāta rāme ca vanam āśrite
verses.translation: "O, king! O, father! Who is supposed to see the welfare and security of your city of Ayodhya, while you have departed for heaven and while Rama has gone, taking refuge in a forest?"

verses.devanagari:
विधवा पृथिवी राजंस् त्वया हीना न राजते |
हीन चन्द्रा इव रजनी नगरी प्रतिभाति माम्
verses.iast:
vidhavā pṛthivī rājaṃs tvayā hīnā na rājate |
hīna candrā iva rajanī nagarī pratibhāti mām
verses.translation: "O, king! Bereft of you and deprived of its lord, this earth does not look charming. To me, this city is looking like a night without a moon."

verses.devanagari:
एवम् विलपमानम् तम् भरतम् दीन मानसम् |
अब्रवीद् वचनम् भूयो वसिष्ठः तु महान् ऋषिः
verses.iast:
evam vilapamānam tam bharatam dīna mānasam |
abravīd vacanam bhūyo vasiṣṭhaḥ tu mahān ṛṣiḥ
verses.translation: The great sage Vasishta again spoke the following words to that Bharata who was distressed in mind and thus lamenting.

verses.devanagari:
प्रेत कार्याणि यानि अस्य कर्तव्यानि विशाम्पतेः |
तानि अव्यग्रम् महा बाहो क्रियताम् अविचारितम्
verses.iast:
preta kāryāṇi yāni asya kartavyāni viśāmpateḥ |
tāni avyagram mahā bāho kriyatām avicāritam
verses.translation: "O, mighty armed Bharata! Without hesitation or repining, carry out the funeral rites of the king that should be done."

verses.devanagari:
तथा इति भरतः वाक्यम् वसिष्ठस्य अभिपूज्य तत् |
ऋत्विक् पुरोहित आचार्यांस् त्वरयाम् आस सर्वशः
verses.iast:
tathā iti bharataḥ vākyam vasiṣṭhasya abhipūjya tat |
ṛtvik purohita ācāryāṃs tvarayām āsa sarvaśaḥ
verses.translation: "Be it so" answered Bharata and obedient to Vasishta's command, he summoned speedily the appointed priests who were knowing the rules of the funeral rites."

verses.devanagari:
ये तु अग्रतः नर इन्द्रस्याग्नि अगारात् बहिष् कृताः |
ऋत्विग्भिर् याजकैः चैव ते ह्रियन्ते यथा विधि
verses.iast:
ye tu agrataḥ nara indrasyāgni agārāt bahiṣ kṛtāḥ |
ṛtvigbhir yājakaiḥ caiva te hriyante yathā vidhi
verses.translation: The fires of that king were prepared outside the chamber and kindled in accordance with the rituals by the priests and the sacrificial attendants.

verses.devanagari:
शिबिलायाम् अथ आरोप्य राजानम् गत चेतनम् |
बाष्प कण्ठा विमनसः तम् ऊहुः परिचारकाः
verses.iast:
śibilāyām atha āropya rājānam gata cetanam |
bāṣpa kaṇṭhā vimanasaḥ tam ūhuḥ paricārakāḥ
verses.translation: The attendants were choked with tears in their throats and disconsolate in their mind, made the dead king to mount on a small palanquin and carried it away.

verses.devanagari:
हिरण्यम् च सुवर्णम् च वासांसि विविधानि च |
प्रकिरन्तः जना मार्गम् नृपतेर् अग्रतः ययुः
verses.iast:
hiraṇyam ca suvarṇam ca vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca |
prakirantaḥ janā mārgam nṛpater agrataḥ yayuḥ
verses.translation: The people went along the path, scattering silver, gold and various kinds of clothes in front of the king.

verses.devanagari:
चन्दन अगुरु निर्यासान् सरलम् पद्मकम् तथा |
देव दारूणि च आहृत्य चिताम् चक्रुस् तथा अपरे
गन्धान् उच्च अवचामः च अन्यांस् तत्र दत्त्वा अथ भूमिपम् |
ततः सम्वेशयाम् आसुः चिता मध्ये तम् ऋत्विजः
verses.iast:
candana aguru niryāsān saralam padmakam tathā |
deva dārūṇi ca āhṛtya citām cakrus tathā apare
gandhān ucca avacāmḥ ca anyāṃs tatra dattvā atha bhūmipam |
tataḥ samveśayām āsuḥ citā madhye tam ṛtvijaḥ
verses.translation: In the same manner, some others brought sandal wood, sweet aloes, different fragrant essences, with leaps of Sarala Padmaka and Devadaru woods and many other kinds of fragrant substances, went there and threw them into the funeral pile. Thereafter the appointed priests caused the king's body to lie down there in the midst of the funeral pyre.

glosses.meaning: in the midst of the funeral pile.

verses.devanagari:
तथा हुत अशनम् हुत्वा जेपुस् तस्य तदा ऋत्विजः |
जगुः च ते यथा शास्त्रम् तत्र सामानि सामगाः
verses.iast:
tathā huta aśanam hutvā jepus tasya tadā ṛtvijaḥ |
jaguḥ ca te yathā śāstram tatra sāmāni sāmagāḥ
verses.translation: Then, those priests engaged for the benefit of the king poured oblations into the fire and recited sacred texts (relevant to the funeral rites). Those among the priests, who could recite the hymns of Samaveda, chanted them according to the rules.

glosses.meaning: engaged for the bereft of the king
those among the priests who could recite the hymns of Samaveda

verses.devanagari:
शिबिकाभिः च यानैः च यथा अर्हम् तस्य योषितः |
नगरान् निर्ययुस् तत्र वृद्धैः परिवृताः तदा
verses.iast:
śibikābhiḥ ca yānaiḥ ca yathā arham tasya yoṣitaḥ |
nagarān niryayus tatra vṛddhaiḥ parivṛtāḥ tadā
verses.translation: Then, his ladies, encircled by elders mounted palanquins or other vehicles, as deserving and departed from the city to that place.

verses.devanagari:
प्रसव्यम् च अपि तम् चक्रुर् ऋत्विजो अग्नि चितम् नृपम् |
स्त्रियः च शोक सम्तप्ताः कौसल्या प्रमुखाः तदा
verses.iast:
prasavyam ca api tam cakrur ṛtvijo agni citam nṛpam |
striyaḥ ca śoka samtaptāḥ kausalyā pramukhāḥ tadā
verses.translation: Then, the appointed priests as well as Kausalya and other women who were tormented with grief, circumambulated in anti clockwise direction that king who was lying on a funeral pile.

glosses.meaning: who was lying on a funeral pile.

verses.devanagari:
क्रौन्चीनाम् इव नारीणाम् निनादः तत्र शुश्रुवे |
आर्तानाम् करुणम् काले क्रोशन्तीनाम् सहस्रशः
verses.iast:
krauncīnām iva nārīṇām ninādaḥ tatra śuśruve |
ārtānām karuṇam kāle krośantīnām sahasraśaḥ
verses.translation: At that time the crying sounds of thousands of women, pitiably weeping with agony, were heard like the sounds of female curlew birds.

glosses.meaning: like the sounds of female curlew birds.

verses.devanagari:
ततः रुदन्त्यो विवशा विलप्य च पुनः पुनः |
यानेभ्यः सरयू तीरम् अवतेरुर् वर अन्गनाः
verses.iast:
tataḥ rudantyo vivaśā vilapya ca punaḥ punaḥ |
yānebhyaḥ sarayū tīram avaterur vara anganāḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, the lamenting ladies deprived of their grit wept again and again and descended from their vehicles at the bank of Sarayu River.

glosses.meaning: at the bank of Sarayu River.

verses.devanagari:
कृत उदकम् ते भरतेन सार्धम् |
नृप अन्गना मन्त्रि पुरोहिताः च |
पुरम् प्रविश्य अश्रु परीत नेत्रा |
भूमौ दश अहम् व्यनयन्त दुह्खम्
verses.iast:
kṛta udakam te bharatena sārdham |
nṛpa anganā mantri purohitāḥ ca |
puram praviśya aśru parīta netrā |
bhūmau daśa aham vyanayanta duhkham
verses.translation: Along with Bharata, the royal women, the ministers and family priests offered their oblations with water and entered the city with their eyes filled in tears and spent ten days with great difficulty by sleeping on bare floor.

glosses.meaning: with their eyes filled in tears
